messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: HIGH severity alert fired for service=dedicated-gpu-west1 pool=gpu-pool-7 — "cuda alloc failure" spike (threshold 5m). Pager: @sam @julia :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: Alert ID PD-88271 created, escalation policy: oncall-eng -> level2 -> pm. http://pd.example/PD-88271

sam: acked. I'm on it. Starting preliminary triage.

maria: saw similar signs earlier this morning but quieted. Any customer errors?

sam: yes, we see increased 5xx from dedicated tenants — logs show CUDA_MEM_ALLOC failures and occasional SIGBUS in driver. Sample: `E [kernel] cuda: failed to allocate 12345678 bytes (out of memory)`

kevin: pulling host metrics now — `nvidia-smi` on gpu-node-17 shows 98% memory used by processes: PID 8243 (model-server), PID 9120 (batcher). Attachting snippet:
```
| GPU | Mem-Usage | Processes |
|  0  | 24906MiB / 25088MiB | model-server (8243) 93%
```

julia: can we drain that node and move live traffic? If it's fragmentation the restart may be required.

sam: agree. Initiating graceful drain for gpu-node-17. Command: `kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m`

maria: also starting reroute: marking pool `gpu-pool-7` as degraded in routing so new requests hit fallback pool `gpu-pool-7b` (lower-cost variant). `redwoodctl routing set pool-status gpu-pool-7 degraded --reason "OOM spike"`

cs-ops: FYI customers AcmeCorp and BetaStream are reporting higher latencies and some request failures. I'm messaging them that we're investigating and may route to fallback capacity.

sam: drain in progress — pods being evicted. Watching for long-running KV cache processes that hold GPU memory. If they don't exit, we'll force-restart container runtime.

kevin: noticed a repeated allocation pattern from model-server PID 8243 that didn't free >30s after request finish — looks like fragmented allocations: driver returns `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` but process doesn't crash. Could be driver-level leak.

julia: patch plan: 1) drain node; 2) restart nvidia driver/service on node; 3) evict lingering containers; 4) scale up fallback pool. If restart fails, we'll reprovision node.

sam: drain completed, but one pod `model-server-8243` stuck terminating. Running `crictl stop 8243` to force.

maria: scaling fallback pool now: `redwoodctl pool scale --pool dedicated-west1-fallback --add 3` — should absorb traffic in ~90s.

pagerduty-bot: PD-88271 acknowledged by sam at 1769554330. Escalation suspended.

kevin: did a driver restart: `sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver` on gpu-node-17. Kernel logs show transient `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus` then recovered. After restart, memory freed. Running `nvidia-smi` now shows free memory.

sam: rebalancing: bringing back healthy pods to the pool. Running health checks on model servers.

cs-ops: customers notified: AcmeCorp sees reduced errors, BetaStream still seeing occasional failures — looks like some long-running sessions were served from the stuck container. They requested a postmortem.

maria: quick note — we should check model-server's custom allocator flags; maybe enabling `--gpu-malloc-threshold=low` would reduce fragmentation. Filing a follow-up ticket.

julia: adding runbook actions: increase `oom-alert` moving window to 3m->2m? Actually we need to reduce noise but catch bursts earlier. Also add a probe to detect long-lived allocations >2m.

kevin: checking node reprovision logs — no disk issues. Suspect driver bug combined with model fragmentation under burst load. Captured kernel dmesg excerpt: `Kernel: NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus` and `cuda: mmap failed: Cannot allocate memory`

sam: summary for PD ticket: root cause suspected GPU driver+allocator fragmentation during burst leading to repeated cudaMalloc failures and one stuck container preventing eviction. Mitigation: drained node, restarted nvidia-driver, forced stuck container stop, scaled fallback pool to absorb traffic, routed new requests away from pool. Impact: 2 dedicated customers experienced elevated 5xx and latency for ~6-12 minutes (AcmeCorp partially, BetaStream heavier).

pagerduty-bot: PD-88271 status updated -> resolved (mitigated) by sam at 1769554505.

julia: follow-ups: (1) create postmortem with timeline and remediation, (2) add health-check to detect long GPU allocations and auto-evict after 2m, (3) test nvidia-driver upgrade in staging, (4) evaluate allocator flags on model-server images.

cs-ops: I'll schedule customer outreach and draft a short incident note for AcmeCorp/BetaStream.

maria: creating GitHub issue INFRA-1409 for the driver+allocator investigation and linking traces/logs.

sam: closing thread here. If anyone sees repeat alerts in next 24h please re-open PD and ping. :thumbsup:
